sentences.text: 1 Jabalpur, Dated : 04-09-2019
Shri Vasant Danial with Shri Ashish Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Sharad Singh, learned P.L. for the respondent No.1/State.
Heard on question of admission.
This revision is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 16316/2019, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.

T he revision has been preferred by the applicant against judgment dated 27.08.2019 passed by VIIth Additional Sessions Judge District Jabalpur (M.P.) in Criminal Appeal No. 145/2018, arising out of judgment and findings dated 03.05.2018 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jatara District Jabalpur (MP) in Criminal Case No. 3114/2008.

entities.text: VIIth Additional Sessions Judge District Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jatara District Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Applicant has been convicted by the trial Court for the offences punishable under Sections 50(1)/7(3)/16(1)(a)(ii) and Section 7(i) r/w 16(I)(a)
(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 month with fine of Rs.
500/- and 1 year with fine of Rs. 5000/-.
Default stipulation has also been imposed by trial Court.

In appeal, the learned appellate Court has acquitted the present petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 7(i) r/w 16(I)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and affirmed the findings of trial Court with regard to offence punishable under Section 50(1)/7(3)/16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

As per prosecution case is that on 08.04.2008 committee constituted by District Administration along with SDM Gohalpur has inspected Murli Dairy situated at Kandra Kheda Pariyat Jabalpur where applicant found present.
On asking about the license same was not produced by the applicant.

On the suspicious of adulteration of milk, the committee has purchased 1500 ml milk from applicant Amrit Lal Makhija vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170877499/
1 and same were sealed as per procedure.

entities.text: Amrit Lal Makhija vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pnachnama has also been prepared and same was duly signed by witnesses.
The sample were sent to Public Analyzer, State Food Laboratories, bhopal for analysis.
The part of sample has also been sent to Local Health Officer, Jabalpur.

On 14.07.2008, a report has been received from Deputy Director Food and Drug Administration and according to it the sample which was seized from the possession of present applicant is found adulterated.
L e a r n e d counsel for the applicant/accused submits that 2 CRR-4317-2019 applicants/accused are innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He is in jail since 27.08.2018.
He further submits that both the Courts below erred in convicting the applicant whereas there is no offence is made out against him.
It may be seen that from the record that the sample was taken on 08.04.2008 and the public analyst has dispatched his report on 14.05.2008.
Thereafter, the complaint case filed on 21.08.2008 after passing more then 4 months from taking sample.
He further submit that the self life of the milk is not more than three months under refrigerating condition.
In the present case, the complaint itself was filed beyond the reasonable period, applicant can not be held guilty.
He further submits that the Food Inspector did not homogenize the milk while taking it sample and because of it the milk fat was found deficit in the milk.
The applicant has a license which was expired on 31.03.2008 i.e. 8 days prior to the inspection and applicant has already applied for its renewal.
These fact was overlooked by the learned Appellant Court and convicted the applicant.
The prosecution has failed to proved its case even then both the Courts have convicted the applicant.
thus there is possibility to get success in this revision petition.
Final hearing of this revision will take time.
If the applicant is not released on bail, the purpose of filing this application will be frustrated.
Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the applicant may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
In support of his contention he has relied the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan passed in Criminal Appeal No. 214-2015/2016.

entities.text: Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application.

After hearing rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and looking to the whole facts and circumstances of the case and fact that the learned appellate Court has acquitted the present petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 7(i) r/w 16(I)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
This revision is of year 2019 and it will take time to its final disposal.

But, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicant and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No. 16316/2019 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.
The custodial sentence awarded to the applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision.

Applicant-Amrit Lal Makhija released from custody subject to their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

The applicant shall appear and mark his presence before trial Court on 14.11.2019 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates as 3 CRR-4317-2019 may be given in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
